name: RRB NTPC (Graduate)
fullName: Railway Recruitment Boards – Non-Technical Popular Categories (Graduate Level)
frequency: Annual (as per RRB calendar; separate Graduate and Undergraduate CENs)
approxCandidates: ≈50–60 lakh applicants per graduate-level cycle (approx.; exact figure for CEN 06/2025 not officially confirmed)
eligibility: Graduate degree from a recognised university; 18–33 yrs (age relaxation as per rules)

notification.summary: Current graduate-level cycle is CEN 06/2025 (5,810 posts such as Goods Train Manager, Station Master, Chief Commercial-cum-Ticket Supervisor, Senior Clerk-cum-Typist). CBT 1 was held 16–27 March 2026, CBT 1 result was declared on 11 June 2026 and CBT 2 was scheduled for 10 July 2026; CBAT/typing skill test and DV are the remaining stages. A fresh graduate-level CEN is expected under the next RRB calendar but had not been notified as of the check date.

pattern.notes: No sectional time limit. Negative marking of 1/3 mark per wrong answer. CBT 1 is qualifying (shortlisting for CBT 2); marks are normalised across shifts. Minimum qualifying percentage: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC 30%, ST 25%. PwBD scribe candidates get 120 minutes.

trendAnalysis.summary: Across the 2024–25 (CEN 05/2024) and March 2026 (CEN 06/2025) graduate CBT 1 shifts, overall difficulty has been easy-to-moderate. General Awareness is the deciding section: memory-based analyses rate it the toughest, with 10–16 current-affairs questions per shift (last 6–12 months: schemes, sports, awards, summits) followed by science, history and polity (specific Articles/amendments). Mathematics is calculation-heavy but conceptually basic (percentage, SI/CI, profit-loss, time-work, mensuration, simple trigonometry). Reasoning is the most scoring section with analogies, series, coding-decoding, syllogism and short puzzles. Good attempts for graduate shifts are reported around 78–88 out of 100.

resources.notes: RRBs do not keep a permanent PYQ archive. After each CBT the question papers, provisional answer keys and candidate response sheets are published for a limited objection window via the regional RRB websites (e.g. https://www.rrbcdg.gov.in, linked from https://www.rrbapply.gov.in). Some cycles also provide a mock-test link on regional RRB sites shortly before the CBT. Shift-wise memory-based papers are available from coaching publishers (unofficial).

questions.question: India observes 'National Space Day' every year on 23 August to commemorate which event?
options: Launch of Aryabhata, India's first satellite
Soft landing of Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander on the Moon
Launch of the Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter) Mission
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander soft-landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023; the Government of India declared 23 August as National Space Day.

questions.question: At the G20 Leaders' Summit held in New Delhi in September 2023, which organisation was admitted as a permanent member of the G20?
questions.explanation: Under India's presidency, the African Union was made a permanent member of the G20 at the New Delhi Summit (9–10 September 2023).

questions.question: Which Indian shooter won two bronze medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics, becoming the first Indian after Independence to win two medals at a single Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10 m air pistol and in the 10 m air pistol mixed team event (with Sarabjot Singh) at Paris 2024.

questions.question: Who proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) at Singapore in October 1943?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind on 21 October 1943 in Singapore.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT part of the combined forces that fought against the East India Company in the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
questions.explanation: At Buxar the Company defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Siraj-ud-Daulah had been killed after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

questions.question: The Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription), composed by the court poet Harisena, describes the achievements of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Harisena, court poet of Samudragupta, composed the Prayag Prashasti engraved on the Allahabad pillar describing Samudragupta's conquests.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976), on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, inserted Part IV-A (Article 51A) with Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution can the President proclaim a Financial Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency; Article 352 is National Emergency and Article 356 is President's Rule in a State.

questions.question: The idea of a 'Concurrent List' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: The Concurrent List (and joint sitting of Parliament) was borrowed from Australia; Directive Principles came from Ireland and the federation with a strong Centre from Canada.

questions.question: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan (about 3.42 lakh km²) is the largest state by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.question: The Nathu La pass, an important trade route between India and China (Tibet), is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Nathu La lies on the Sikkim–Tibet border and is used for border trade and the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. It does not pass through Odisha.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃. Na₂CO₃ is washing soda (in its decahydrate form).

questions.question: Which part of the human brain is mainly responsible for maintaining posture and balance of the body?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum (part of the hindbrain) coordinates voluntary movements and maintains posture and equilibrium.

questions.question: A lens has a power of −2.5 D. Which of the following correctly describes it?
options: Concave lens of focal length 40 cm
Convex lens of focal length 40 cm
Concave lens of focal length 25 cm
Convex lens of focal length 25 cm
questions.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/(−2.5) m = −0.4 m = −40 cm. A negative focal length means a concave (diverging) lens.

questions.question: In Mendel's dihybrid cross between pure-breeding round-yellow and wrinkled-green pea plants, the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F₂ generation is:
questions.explanation: Selfing the F₁ (RrYy) gives 9 round-yellow : 3 round-green : 3 wrinkled-yellow : 1 wrinkled-green.

questions.question: In India, the policy repo rate is decided by:
options: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI
questions.explanation: Since 2016 the six-member Monetary Policy Committee constituted under the RBI Act fixes the policy repo rate.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented across India with effect from:
questions.explanation: GST, introduced through the 101st Constitutional Amendment, came into force on 1 July 2017.

questions.question: Kathakali is a classical dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Kathakali is from Kerala; Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu, Odissi from Odisha and Manipuri from Manipur.

questions.question: The Durand Cup, one of the oldest tournaments in Asia, is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Durand Cup, first held in 1888, is a football tournament.

questions.question: In most Windows applications, which keyboard shortcut is used to undo the last action?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes; Ctrl + Y redoes, Ctrl + X cuts and Ctrl + U underlines.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, has its seat at:
questions.explanation: The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace at The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question: World Environment Day is observed every year on:
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is on 5 June; 22 April is Earth Day and 16 September is World Ozone Day.

questions.question: Which of the following biosphere reserves is located in Tamil Nadu?
questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar is in Tamil Nadu; Simlipal is in Odisha, Nokrek in Meghalaya and Pachmarhi in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 7³⁵?
questions.explanation: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in the cycle 7, 9, 3, 1. 35 = 4×8 + 3, so the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, i.e. 3.

questions.question: What is the least number that must be added to 2497 so that the sum is exactly divisible by 13?
questions.explanation: 13 × 192 = 2496, so 2497 leaves remainder 1. Add 13 − 1 = 12 to get 2509 = 13 × 193.

questions.question: Simplify: 48 ÷ 6 × 4 − 3² + 5
The LCM of two numbers is 360 and their HCF is 12. If one of the numbers is 72, the other number is:
questions.explanation: Product of numbers = HCF × LCM = 12 × 360 = 4320. Other number = 4320 ÷ 72 = 60.

questions.question: What is the value of 35% of 240 + 15% of 160?
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: Required reduction = 25/(100 + 25) × 100 = 20%.

questions.question: ₹7,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. What is B's share?
questions.explanation: 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4 = 6 : 4 : 3 (multiplying by 12). Total 13 parts; one part = 7800/13 = 600. B gets 4 × 600 = ₹2,400.

questions.question: The average of 11 numbers is 36. The average of the first 6 numbers is 32 and that of the last 6 numbers is 40. What is the 6th number?
A shopkeeper marks an article 25% above its cost price and then allows a discount of 12%. What is his profit percentage?
A trader sells two articles for ₹990 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall result?
questions.explanation: CP of first = 990/1.1 = 900; CP of second = 990/0.9 = 1100. Total CP = 2000, total SP = 1980, so loss = ₹20 (1%).

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹6,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
What is the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on ₹12,000 at 10% per annum for 3 years?
A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: Work done in 4 days = 4 × (1/12 + 1/18) = 4 × 5/36 = 5/9. Remaining = 4/9; B needs (4/9) × 18 = 8 days.

questions.question: A train 240 m long is running at 72 km/h. How long will it take to cross a signal pole?
Two trains of lengths 150 m and 210 m are running in opposite directions on parallel tracks at 60 km/h and 48 km/h. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. Distance = 150 + 210 = 360 m. Time = 360/30 = 12 s.

questions.question: What is the curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
If x + 1/x = 5, then what is the value of x³ + 1/x³?
If sin θ = 3/5, where θ is an acute angle, then what is the value of tan θ + sec θ?
questions.explanation: cos θ = 4/5, so tan θ = 3/4 and sec θ = 5/4. Sum = 8/4 = 2.

questions.question: Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is used to write; similarly a knife is used to cut (tool : function).

questions.question: Select the number that completes the analogy. 7 : 50 :: 9 : ?
questions.explanation: 7² + 1 = 50; similarly 9² + 1 = 82.

questions.question: Select the odd number out: 23, 29, 37, 51
questions.explanation: 23, 29 and 37 are prime numbers; 51 = 3 × 17 is composite.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
questions.explanation: Terms are n² − 1 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 → next is 7² − 1 = 48. (Differences 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.)

questions.question: Find the next term: 1, 2, 6, 21, 88, ?
If CAT is coded as DBU, how will DOG be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted one place forward: D→E, O→P, G→H.

questions.question: In a certain code, MANGO is written as OCPIQ. How will APPLE be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved two places forward: A→C, P→R, P→R, L→N, E→G.

questions.question: If '+' means '×', '×' means '−', '−' means '÷' and '÷' means '+', what is the value of 16 − 4 + 3 ÷ 8 × 5?
Pointing to a man, Riya (a girl) said, 'He is the only son of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the man related to Riya?
questions.explanation: The only son of Riya's grandfather is her father. The only son of her father is her brother.

questions.question: Aman walks 8 m north, turns right and walks 5 m, turns right again and walks 14 m, then turns right and walks 5 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Taking the start as (0, 0): north 8 → (0, 8); east 5 → (5, 8); south 14 → (5, −6); west 5 → (0, −6). He is 6 m south of the start.

questions.question:
Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red.
Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. Some flowers are roses.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: 'All roses are flowers' converts to 'Some flowers are roses', so II follows. The red flowers need not include any rose, so I does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: No pen is a book. All books are copies.
Conclusions: I. Some copies are not pens. II. No copy is a pen.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: The copies that are books cannot be pens, so 'Some copies are not pens' is definite. Copies outside the book region may or may not be pens, so II is not certain.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. R sits in the middle. P sits at the extreme left. T sits to the immediate right of R. Q is not an immediate neighbour of P. Who sits second from the left end?
questions.explanation: Positions 1–5 from left: P = 1, R = 3, T = 4. Q and S take 2 and 5; Q cannot be next to P, so Q = 5 and S = 2.

questions.question: J, K, L, M, N and O sit in a row facing north. K sits third from the left end. Exactly two people sit between K and N. J sits to the immediate left of O. L does not sit at either end. M sits at one of the ends. Who sits exactly between L and J?
questions.explanation: K = 3, so N = 6 (two people between them). M must be at an end, and position 6 is taken, so M = 1. J–O must be adjacent among 2, 4, 5 → J = 4, O = 5. L = 2. Order: M L K J O N, so K sits between L and J.

questions.question: In a group of 60 people, 35 like tea, 30 like coffee and 10 like both. How many people like neither tea nor coffee?
questions.explanation: People liking at least one = 35 + 30 − 10 = 55. Neither = 60 − 55 = 5.

questions.question:
Statement: The railway has introduced online ticket booking to reduce queues at ticket counters.
Conclusions: I. Online booking may reduce crowding at ticket counters. II. All passengers will now book their tickets only online.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: The stated purpose directly supports I. Nothing says counters are closed or that every passenger will switch, so II does not follow.

questions.question: If the English alphabet is written in reverse order, which letter will be 7th from the left?
questions.explanation: Reverse order: Z, Y, X, W, V, U, T … The 7th letter is T (equivalently 27 − 7 = 20th letter of the normal order).

questions.question: 15 August 2026 falls on a Saturday. On which day of the week did 15 August 2025 fall?
questions.explanation: From 15 Aug 2025 to 15 Aug 2026 there are 365 days (February 2026 has 28 days), i.e. 52 weeks + 1 day. So 15 Aug 2025 was one day before Saturday: Friday.
